new_mathematics.theorem: If an original-coordinate square cross block satisfies BB^T=sigma^2 I_m with m>4, then ||p||inf <= [e sqrt(2)/(4 sigma)] m/(m-4), with continuous C0 density.
new_mathematics.family: A_k=H^(tensor k), n=2^k>=16, all eigenvalues modulus one, first-bit cross block BB^T=(1/2)I; therefore ||p||inf<=e n/[2(n-8)]<=e for every admissible product input.
new_mathematics.delocalization: An explicit orthonormal +1 three-frame has max row leverage ((2+sqrt(2))/4)^(k-3)*(7/16+5sqrt(2)/32), tending to zero.
new_mathematics.local_obstruction: Every fixed r x r physical principal block has operator norm at most r/sqrt(n), so no bounded-size uniformly nondegenerate principal-block reduction is exhaustive.
new_mathematics.partner_application: For diag(1,[[0,O],[O^T,0]]) with O=I-(2/3)11^T, q=1,gamma=1 gives theta=3/2,D=8; partner theorem with s=3/2 yields ||p||inf<=6 sqrt(e sqrt(2))=11.7640263946... although direct ridge L-infinity inversion fails.

next_step: Prove an exhaustive original-coordinate alternative after bounded selected-mass conditioning between a uniformly scaled localized/grouped smoothing certificate and a ridge cut with max diag K<=q/2 and theta>2q, or theta>q when a usable pivot is present; preserve arbitrary complementary spectrum and known bank counterexamples.
